title: Signs in Creation
subtitle: Sky, earth, rain, animals and the human body as signs of the one Creator and of the resurrection, and the modern argument over the Quran and science
summary: The Quran uses one word, aya, for a verse of its text and for a sign in the world, and it points to the world constantly: the alternation of night and day, the ships on the sea, the rain that revives dead land, the bee, the camel, the child growing in the womb. Each is a sign “for people who reflect” of two things: that God alone made and rules everything, so He alone should be worshiped; and that the One who made you and brings dead earth to life can raise you from the dead. The Psalms and Paul make the first argument in much the same way. Since the 1970s many Muslim writers have also read some of these verses as foretelling modern science: the heavens and earth split from “one mass” as the Big Bang, “We are expanding it” as the expanding universe, the stages of the embryo, the barrier between fresh and salt water. Others, Muslim scholars among them, answer that the verses speak in the words and picture of the world of their own time, where the sky is a raised ceiling without visible pillars, mountains are pegs that keep the earth from shifting, and the sun sets in a murky spring. The notes mark the verses at the center of that argument.

refs.label: “Signs for people who understand”
refs.note: The heavens and earth, night and day, ships on the sea, rain, animals, winds, and clouds “disposed between the sky and the earth.”

refs.label: “Our Lord, You did not create this in vain”
refs.note: Those who remember God standing, sitting and lying down, and reflect on creation.

refs.label: “And of His signs …”
refs.note: Six signs in a row: made from dust; spouses and love; the diversity of “your languages and colors”; sleep; lightning and rain; the heaven and earth standing by His command, “and then, when He calls you out of the earth, you will emerge at once.”

refs.label: “In your own creation, and in the creatures He scattered”
“We will show them Our proofs on the horizons, and in their very souls”
“Is there another god with God?”
refs.note: Asked five times, after each work of God: rain, a habitable earth, the answer to the one in need, guidance by the stars, the creation and its repetition.

refs.label: “The heavens and the earth were one mass, and We tore them apart”
refs.note: “And We made from water every living thing.” The sky is “a protected ceiling,” and sun and moon each float in an orbit. Many modern Muslim writers read 21:30 as the Big Bang; classical commentators read it of the sky and earth separated at creation, as in Genesis, or of rain split from the sky and plants from the earth.

refs.label: “We constructed the universe with power, and We are expanding it”
refs.note: Itani's translation follows the modern reading, the expanding universe. Pickthall: “We it is Who make the vast extent (thereof).” The Arabic word (musi'un) can mean making wide or having ample means.

refs.label: “He … raised the heavens without pillars that you can see”
refs.note: Also 31:10. Job speaks of “the pillars of heaven.”

refs.label: Seven heavens in layers; the lower adorned with lamps
refs.note: “You see no discrepancy in the creation of the Compassionate. Look again. Can you see any cracks?” The stars are also “missiles against the devils.”

refs.label: “The sun runs towards its destination … Each floats in an orbit”
refs.note: “The sun is not to overtake the moon, nor is the night to outpace the day.”

refs.label: The sun radiant, the moon a light, “that you may know the number of years”
refs.note: The Islamic calendar is lunar, twelve months of twenty-nine or thirty days, so Ramadan moves through the seasons.

refs.label: “Do not bow down to the sun, nor to the moon”
Stars “that you may be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea”
“Did We not make the earth a cradle? And the mountains pegs?”
refs.note: Eleven questions, from the earth to the gardens. Mountains as pegs, set “lest it shifts with you” (16:15, 21:31, 31:10), are read by some modern writers as the deep roots of mountains, and by others as a picture of a flat earth held steady.

refs.label: “Do they not look at the camels—how they are created?”
refs.note: “And at the sky—how it is raised? And at the mountains—how they are installed? And at the earth—how it is spread out?”

refs.label: “Are you more difficult to create, or the heaven?”
refs.note: “And the earth after that He spread.” Commentators debated how this order, heaven then earth, fits 41:9-12, earth then heaven.

refs.label: Two seas, “fresh and sweet” and “salty and bitter,” with a barrier between
refs.note: Also 55:19-22 and 27:61. Read today of where rivers meet the sea.

refs.label: “Irrigated with the same water. We make some taste better than others”
The sun “setting in a murky spring”
refs.note: What Dhul-Qarnayn found at the western edge of his journey. Commentators said it only looked so to him; critics read it as the ancient picture of the world.

groups.title: Rain and growth
groups.note: The Quran's favorite sign: rain on dead land, and the harvest, which “likewise is the resurrection” (50:11).

refs.label: “It is God Who splits the grain and the seed”
refs.note: “Watch their fruits as they grow and ripen.”

refs.label: “From it is drink, and with it grows vegetation”
“A sign for them in the dead land”
refs.note: “Glory be to Him who created all the pairs.”

refs.label: “Let man consider his food”
Clouds piled up, rain and hail
“The winds, bringing advance news of His mercy”
Livestock for warmth, food, beauty and burdens; horses, mules and donkeys
refs.note: “And He creates what you do not know.”

refs.label: Milk “from between waste and blood”
“Your Lord inspired the bee”
refs.note: Honey, “containing healing for the people.” Surah 16 is named “The Bee.”

refs.label: “Communities like you”
refs.note: “There is no animal on land, nor a bird flying with its wings, but are communities like you.”

refs.label: “The birds in formation … each knows its prayer”
“God created every living creature from water”
refs.note: Some crawl, some walk on two feet, some on four.

refs.label: Clay, a drop, a clot, a lump, bones, flesh
refs.note: “Then We produced it into another creature. Most Blessed is God, the Best of Creators.” Modern writers read the stages as embryology revealed ahead of science; critics point out that the Greek physician Galen, in the second century, had described a similar sequence of stages.

refs.label: “From dust, then from a small drop, then from a clinging clot”
refs.note: Given as proof of the resurrection.

refs.label: “In successive formations, in a triple darkness”
“Gushing liquid, issuing from between the backbone and the breastbones”
refs.note: Pickthall: “between the loins and ribs.”

refs.label: “In the best design. Then reduced him to the lowest of the low”
“He created man, and taught him clear expression”
Sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees and animals bow down
refs.note: “… and many of the people. But many are justly deserving of punishment.”

refs.label: “The stars and the trees prostrate themselves”
“Is He who creates like him who does not create?”
refs.note: “If you tried to enumerate the favors of God, you will not be able to count them.”

views.title: Nöldeke's periods
views.note: The signs fill the Meccan surahs, where the Quran argues with those who worshiped other gods and doubted the resurrection.
